newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul stocks close sharply higher on trade surplus.
newsitem.headline: Seoul stocks close sharply higher on trade surplus.

text.p: The first monthly trade surplus in June since December, 1994 fuelled active buying interest across the board, sending the Seoul stock market to a sharply higher close on Tuesday, brokers said.
South Korea's customs-cleared trade swung to a $97.6 million surplus in June from a $426 million deficit a year earlier.
Brokers said investors widely shrugged off North Korea's acceptance of four-nation peace talks with South Korea, the United States and China on August 5.
The composite stock index closed up 12.63 points, or 1.69 percent, to 758.03, off the day's low of 744.67.
"The improved trade figures sparked active buying interest among blue chips, which are the main power of the economy," said Hwang Chang-joong at LG Securities.

The trade ministry said a rise in semiconductor exports and growth in sales of petrochemical and steel products prompted the increase in exports. The June exports rose 9.2 percent to $12.3 billion, marking the third straight monthly rise this year.
"I expected the trade deficit to shrink considerably from this summer on," said Steve Marvin, head of research at Ssangyong Securities. "I think this would become a trend for the rest of the year."
South Korea's consumer price index (CPI) rose 4.0 percent in June on the year, down from a 5.5 percent rise a year earlier.
Among the rising primary blue chips, Samsung Electronics rose 500 won to 71,000 and steelmaker POSCO added 2,400 won to 66,000.
LG Electronics recorded a new 1997 high of 17,800 on the back of active foreign buying interest. It hit the fourth largest trading volume of 815,060 shares.
The largest trading volume was seen in Daewoo Electronics as 1.17 million shares changed hands. It went limit up, gaining 540 won to 7,390.
Hopes for good growth prospects attracted persistent buying interest in LG Information and Communications.
LG Information gained 2,500 won to 112,500, briefly touching a yearly high of 113,500.

Brokers said healthy buying orders spread into financial shares, especially in securities houses, after the index gained eight points in the afternoon session. The securities sub-index rose 86.06 points, or 6.66 percent, to 1,378.37.
Cho Hung Bank rose 270 won at 6,170 with the second largest volume of 1.00 million shares. Daewoo Securities rose up to its upper-limit at 17,300, up 1,200 won.

"As the buying interest was extended across the board, the market seemed to spend too much energy in a short period. I'm questioning whether the market can sustain the upbeat trend tomorrow," said Park Sang-jae at Coryo Securities.
Casey Choe at Union Bank of Switzerland said the market would consolidate further in July.
